title: Four lines of numerals, letters and invented signs in a Syriac-Karshuni miscellany from Midyat (Berlin SBB, Sachau 218, f. 231a)

steps.what: Opened Sachau 218 images 466-468 (ff. 230v-231v) on the SBB IIIF server; METS carries no explicit licence, so nothing is reproduced; the server answers 429 to rapid requests.
Two passes at two scales, arbitrated on the image: 59 signs of 26 shapes in about 13 groups; underlining hooks and the ascenders of line 5 excluded; frozen (transcription.sha256).
Sachau 1899 (archive.org OCR) for the entry and the index of secret scripts; SBB images of Sachau 116 f. 1r and Sachau 93 f. 75 (alphabets, a Syriac atbash table) for key material.

Pre-registered key K1 (numeral-shaped signs = abjad letter values, red dot x10, 0 values adjusted), scored once by Arabic bigrams against 200 random keys: -2.80 on 12 bigrams, rank 12 of 201 (null max -2.49); no group decodes to a whole word. Not supported.

Matched control at integration: 200 held-out Arabic runs of 13 words and 55-63 letters enciphered with K1's design and scored with the true key as K1 was: true key first of 201 in 16 of 200 trials (median rank 12), never 3 whole words. The frozen test had almost no power at this length.
Context: lines 5-9 give a method for knowing whether a sick person will recover; the four lines may be its table of values rather than a cipher. Not tested.

outcome.method_basis: One frozen key (abjad numerals) scored rank 12 of 201 and gave no whole word, so it is not supported; a matched control shows the same test ranks the true key first in only 8% of trials at this length, so the key is not ruled out either; no reading.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt: 59 signs, none given a value

credits.note: transcription of the 59 signs, one pre-registered test of an abjad-numeral key (not supported, rank 12 of 201), matched control showing the test's low power; not read

outcome.notes: Sachau 221 f. 20b (tree script, a different system) is being worked on; no reading of it is offered here.

prior.where: Sachau 1899 vol. 2 pp. 614-615 no. 188 describes the lines, no reading; nothing on DECODE, Tomokiyo or Lasry (catalogue 2943 vetting, PR #706); nothing in our files.

human: Brice Dudout chose the lead and set the rule: transcription and one key test frozen (SHA-256) before any decoding, one run. Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, measured and wrote up; the matched control was added at integration. No human has checked the transcription.
